off.label: Off
off.hint: Default. Native haptics only (channels 2 + 3 of the USB audio stream).

fallback.label: Fallback
fallback.hint: Derived haptic fires only when the game has been silent on the native haptic path for ~1 s. Preserves native HD haptics (Spider-Man Remastered, etc.) while filling in for games that send no haptic data (Ghost of Tsushima on Linux, etc.).

mix.label: Mix
mix.hint: Always add derived haptic on top of native, soft-clipped together. Best for adding more body to games with weak native haptics.

replace.label: Replace
replace.hint: Always use derived; discard native completely. Uniform feel across all games regardless of what they send.

haptics.audioBufferSub: Lower: less audio delay. Higher: steadier audio if it crackles.

remap.unsupported: The connected firmware doesn't support button remapping. Update to the latest OLED Edition firmware on the Flash tab.
remap.verifyFailed: Remap write could not be verified — the device did not confirm the change.

bar.unsaved: Applied to the dongle, not saved yet: changes are lost when it powers off.
bar.saved: All changes saved on the dongle.
bar.profileSaved: Changes go to the profile; normal settings come back when the game closes.
bar.profileUnsaved: Changed here, not saved to the profile yet.

settings.usbHint: These take effect after Reconnect USB (the PC sees the dongle unplug and replug).
settings.speakerLevelSub: 0 = unchanged; above 0 boosts and can clip

lightbar.hint: While charging, the dongle shows an amber pulse in every mode.

slots.title: Pairing slots
slots.hint: Each slot remembers one controller. Switching disconnects the current controller; press PS on the one in the new slot. To pair a new controller into an empty slot, switch to it and hold Create + PS.

triggers.title: Adaptive trigger test
triggers.hint: Pick an effect, then pull L2 and R2. Games override this as soon as they send their own trigger effects.

diag.core1Frozen: Core1 stopped: the audio path is dead until the dongle restarts.

firmware.rebooting: Restarting… press PS on the controller once it's back.
firmware.bootsel: The dongle is now an RP2350 drive. Copy a .uf2 onto it, or unplug it to cancel.
firmware.resetDone: Settings reset to defaults and saved.
firmware.resetHint: Factory reset restores default settings. Pairings and button remaps are kept.
firmware.updateHint: The dongle restarts into its bootloader, gets flashed and restarts on its own. Keep it plugged in; press PS on the controller afterwards.
firmware.checkedCurrent: Checked just now: you're up to date.
firmware.checkedNone: Checked just now: no release has been published yet.
firmware.checkedOffline: Couldn't check: the update server can't be reached (offline?).

usbAccess.label: USB access rule
usbAccess.missing: Not installed (Steam's rules may already cover the dongle)

windowsUsb.hint: Plugged in, the controller is on, and it still never connects? Windows may be holding an old USB setting for it.
windowsUsb.seen: The dongle is plugged in, but Windows hasn't set up its driver.
windowsUsb.done: Repaired. Now unplug the dongle and plug it back in.

step.admin: Windows asks for administrator permission (Windows PowerShell, from Microsoft). Choose No and nothing changes.
step.forget: Windows forgets the USB setting it saved for the dongle's two USB IDs (054C:0CE6 and 054C:0DF2). Nothing else in the registry is touched.
step.entries: It removes Windows' saved device entries for those two IDs. Windows creates them again by itself.
step.replug: You unplug the dongle and plug it back in. Windows sets up its driver from scratch, and the app connects.

update.ready: Version {{version}} is installed. It starts the next time you open the app, or restart now.
update.manual: App update {{version}} is available on the release page.
update.fwDontUnplug: Updating firmware, don't unplug the dongle.
update.fwDone: Firmware updated to {{version}}. Press PS to reconnect the controller.

fwStep.rebooting: Restarting the dongle into its bootloader…
fwStep.verifying: Waiting for the dongle: press PS on the controller to reconnect it.
fwStep.verifyingPress: Flashed. Press PS on the controller: the dongle comes back once a controller connects. If it stays dark, unplug it and plug it back in.

update.askTitle: Keep the app up to date?
update.askBody: New versions can download and install by themselves, checked like every update, and start the next time you open the app. You can change this in App settings.

controller.pairHint: Already paired? Press the PS button. New controller? Hold PS + Create until the light bar flashes; it pairs into the current slot.

games.title: Game setup
games.intro: Checks your launchers for settings that stop adaptive triggers and haptics from reaching games. Checking only reads your settings. Nothing changes until you review the changes and press Apply, and every change can be undone.
games.noLaunchers: No Steam, Heroic or Lutris installation found.
games.protonMissing: Our Proton build isn't installed yet. Windows games need it for adaptive triggers and haptics through the dongle.
games.protonConfirm: This downloads {{name}} ({{size}}) from the project's GitHub release, checks its SHA-256 checksum, and installs it where your launchers look for Proton builds. Existing Proton versions are not changed or removed. Afterwards you choose which launchers and games use it.
games.hidrawOk: games can talk to the controller directly
games.hidrawNo: games can't reach the controller (missing udev rule)
games.envHint: These variables are set outside any launcher, so this app doesn't change them. Remove them from the file named above, then log out and back in.
games.systemRule: A system-wide audio rule forces pro-audio. It's outside your home folder, so this app won't change it.
games.allGood: Everything is set up. Nothing to change.
games.changesHint: Recommended changes are ticked. Untick anything you'd rather keep as it is.
games.reviewHint: These files will be changed. Each one is backed up first, so Undo puts it back exactly as it was.
games.mustClose: {{launcher}} is running. It rewrites these settings when it quits, which would undo the changes, so it has to be closed first.
games.closeGameRunning: A game is still running. Quit the game first, then try again.
games.closeTimeout: {{launcher}} didn't quit within 30 seconds. Quit it yourself, then press Rescan.
games.doneHint: Start the launcher again; it picks up the new settings when it starts.
games.undoBlocked: Close {{launchers}} first: it would overwrite the restored settings when it quits.

label.defaultSteam: Make {{proton}} Steam's default for Windows games
label.audioRule: Turn off the audio rule that forces the controller onto "pro-audio"
label.audioProfile: Switch the controller's audio to the "{{profile}}" profile

why.defaultSteam: Steam currently runs Windows games with {{current}}. Our build is what makes adaptive triggers and haptics work through the dongle. Games you've set to a specific Proton keep their own setting.
why.defaultHeroic: Heroic currently gives new Epic, GOG and Amazon installs {{current}}. This only affects games you install from now on; installed games keep their own setting, and this page checks those one by one.
why.defaultLutris: Lutris currently uses {{current}} for Wine games. Games with their own Wine version keep it.
why.runner: {{support}} It currently runs with {{current}}, which doesn't pass the controller's native features through.
why.runnerMissing: {{game}} is set to {{current}}, which is no longer installed, so the game can't start.
why.steamInput: {{support}} Steam Input is switched on for this game, so Steam translates the controller into a generic gamepad and the game never sees the DualSense. This is the same as Properties → Controller → "Disable Steam Input" in Steam.
why.envSteam: {{vars}} makes Proton present the controller as an Xbox pad, which turns off adaptive triggers. The launch options become: {{options}}
why.envHeroic: {{vars}} makes Proton present the controller as an Xbox pad, which turns off adaptive triggers.
why.audioRule: {{file}} switches the DualSense's audio card to the pro-audio profile, which makes GE-Proton 11 send zero-force triggers and no haptics. The file is renamed to .disabled (not deleted) and the audio service (WirePlumber) restarts, so sound drops for a second.
why.audioProfile: The DualSense's audio card is on "{{profile}}", which makes GE-Proton 11 send zero-force triggers and no haptics. No files change; it's the same as picking the profile in your sound settings.

support.triggers: This game supports the DualSense's adaptive triggers and haptics.

result.stale: This change no longer applies (the setup changed since the last scan).
result.restartFailed: Saved, but restarting the audio service failed: {{error}}

games.envSession: {{variable}} is set in this session's environment
games.consentIntro: Game setup checks Steam, Heroic and Lutris for settings that stop adaptive triggers and haptics from reaching your games. To do that it reads, on this computer only:
games.consentLaunchers: the settings and installed-game lists of Steam, Heroic and Lutris
games.consentAudio: the controller's audio profile and controller access
games.consentProton: which DualSense Proton build is newest, from this project's update feed on GitHub
games.consentPromise: Checking changes nothing, and nothing about your games or settings is sent anywhere. Changes are only made after you review them and press Apply.
games.stopHint: Turns game setup off; it won't read launcher settings again until you allow it.
games.closeFailed: {{launcher}} couldn't be asked to quit. Quit it yourself, then press Rescan.
games.undoConflict: Not undone: {{files}} changed after this was applied (the launcher saved its own settings). Undoing would throw those changes away.

setup.restartingHint: Hold PS + Create on the controller until the light bar flashes. The dongle shows up here once the controller connects (a previously paired controller just needs the PS button).
setup.found: A Pico is ready to set up
setup.offerBundled: Install firmware {{version}}, included with this app (no download needed).
setup.offerOnline: Install firmware {{version}}, the newest published version.
setup.replaces: This replaces whatever is on the Pico now.

setup.driveNote: Your computer may also show it as a drive called RP2350. You don't need to open it.
setup.pairHint: Press PS on the controller. A new controller: hold PS + Create until the light bar flashes (the dongle's screen shows "Pair your DualSense").
setup.whyHidden: The dongle only shows up on this PC once a controller is connected to it.
setup.fwHowTo: To update or reinstall the firmware without a controller: hold the Pico's BOOTSEL button while you plug the dongle in. This screen then offers to install it.
setup.checkedCurrent: The app is up to date ({{version}}).
setup.checkedNewer: App {{version}} is available: see the banner at the top.
setup.checkFailed: Couldn't check for updates. Are you online?

live.speaker: Speaker

go.intro: Click a part of the drawing with your mouse, or pick a setting here:

triggers.title: Adaptive triggers
triggers.sub: Try the effects on L2 / R2

go.buttons: To remap a button or stick, click it on the drawing.
go.bodyHint: Haptics: strength and Audio Auto Haptics

live.autoInstallSub: Downloads and checks them in the background; the new version starts the next time you open the app
live.hapticSilent: Silent: nothing is sending haptics right now. It moves while a game plays HD haptics, or with Audio Auto Haptics on while sound plays.

live.hardwareAccelerationSub: Draws with the graphics card: smoother, and needed for blur and glass effects. Turns itself off if the graphics card crashes.

tour.helpHint: The quick guided tour from the first start.

welcome.title: Welcome!
welcome.body: Let's take a one-minute tour, with your controller in your hands. Press ✕ to continue and ○ to go back. Esc or Skip tour stops it any time.
welcome.bodyAsk: A one-minute tour, with your controller in your hands. Esc or Skip tour stops it any time.

press.title: This is your controller, live
press.body: Press a few different buttons on your controller and watch them light up here.
press.done: Nice! Everything you press shows up here.

trigger.title: Now the triggers
trigger.body: Now pull a trigger, L2 or R2, all the way down. Feel anything?
trigger.done: Feel that? That's an adaptive trigger: it pushes back, then snaps through. Games use it for guns, bows and brakes.

click.title: Set things up with the mouse
click.body: Click the glowing light strip beside the touchpad with your mouse. Every part of the drawing opens its own settings.

panel.title: Settings open here
panel.body: Changes go to the dongle right away, so you see, hear and feel them as you go. ✕ closes the panel.

list.title: Or pick from the list
list.body: Not sure where something lives on the controller? Every setting is also here, one click away. » hides this panel for a bigger controller.

save.title: Keep what you like
save.body: Changes are live but temporary. Save to dongle keeps them after it powers off; Revert goes back to what's saved.

top.title: The dongle, your games, and help
top.body: Dongle: firmware updates, the OLED, power and USB. Games: get Steam and other launchers ready for triggers and haptics (Linux). About: what's new and the guide. ⚙: the app's own settings.

finish.title: You're all set
finish.body: Have fun! You can replay this tour any time from ⚙ App settings.

tour.voiceAsk: Want her to talk you through it? She speaks only through your controller's speaker; you can change it any time in ⚙ App settings.

data.title: Everything, live
data.body: Down here: the sticks, triggers, motion, battery and the link, all as numbers and graphs, as your controller moves.

tour.keepPlaying: Keep playing as long as you like; hold ✕ when you're ready.
tour.holdHint: Hold ✕ to skip this step, or hold ○ to go back.

narrator.voiceSub: Short spoken lines for the tour and app events, only through your controller's speaker
narrator.captionsSub: Show her words on screen while she speaks (and the short confirmations as text when the voice is off)

settings2.reduceMotionSub: No moving background, pulsing or animations (also on when your system asks for it)

dev.title: Developer
dev.hint: Preview another controller model and colorway to check the app's colors. Only changes what the app shows; nothing is sent to the dongle. Ctrl+Shift+D hides this card.
dev.hdrHint: Display reports HDR: {{state}}. A swatch that works glows clearly brighter than the white reference.
dev.updatesHint: Show an app and firmware update in each state, to check how they look. Nothing is downloaded or flashed.

knobs.cardOpacitySub: Lower lets the background show through the cards
knobs.backdropDimSub: How much the page darkens the game art
knobs.backdropBlurSub: Softer or sharper game art behind the page
knobs.depthSub: Shadow strength under cards and the controller (0 = flat)

calib.title: Calibration
calib.shortcut: Stick drift, deadzones, trigger travel, gyro
calib.intro: Corrects stick drift, deadzones, trigger travel and the gyro's zero inside the dongle, for every game. Nothing is written to the controller; Reset undoes it.
calib.needsFirmware: Update the dongle's firmware to calibrate.
calib.noInput: No input from the controller during that step. Try again.
calib.measured: Measured. Check the previews, then Save.

step.edges: Roll both sticks slowly around their edges
step.triggers: Press both triggers all the way, then let go
step.gyro: Put the controller down and don't touch it

calib.deadzoneSub: Movement near the center that's ignored (stops drift)
calib.outerSub: How far the stick must go to count as fully pushed
calib.saveHint: Saved in the dongle's own memory; it applies to every game right away.
calib.forSlot: For the controller in pairing slot {{slot}}; each slot keeps its own.
calib.missed: Not measured, so the old values were kept: {{parts}}. Go all the way on those and measure again.

hdr.label: HDR lighting (experimental)
hdr.sub: The lightbar glows brighter than white on an HDR display, like the real LEDs. Needs hardware acceleration; applies at restart.

grips.testHint: A short rumble on that grip at its strength now (the trigger tests don't use these: L2 and R2 have their own motors).

channel.label: Update channel
channel.devHint: Development builds of the app and the firmware, before they're released: newer, and less tested. You also get every stable release. Back to stable installs the latest stable app and firmware.
